items.evidence: Under "## The bottom line" the overview runs "**1. What FRUS answers directly.** In the printed record corruption works on U.S. policy in three ways..." (line 5), then "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** *Where the printed documents came from:* eight of the 28 came from the Department of State's Central Decimal File..." (line 21), then "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** (a) *The investigations themselves.*..." (line 41). Scope and "Decisions this needs from you" follow, and "## Findings" begins only at line 71.

Every figure carries its set: "The argument rests on 28 documents from 12 volumes, dated 1947 to 1978, chosen from roughly 2,200 documents across the whole 553-volume series that mention corruption"; "The scoping set is the 2,186 documents, out of 311,429, that use any form of the word"; "A hand-coded evenly spaced sample of 40 found 36"; "Only 9 of the 2,186 use it for garbled telegram text"; "In the 1920s and 1930s about two documents in a thousand mention it. In the 1960s and 1970s about sixteen in a thousand do"; "found in 552 of them" (of all 553 volumes). A grep finds no % or "percent" anywhere. Closest call: "In those volumes it is about nine times as frequent as elsewhere" is a ratio rather than a count, but its comparator (the other volumes) is named, so it is neither a bare percentage nor a figure without a base.

Lines 148–150: "Also cited above: the Strauss and Starfighter memorandum (Volume E–15, Part 2, Document 292), the staff meeting (Volume E–9, Part 2, Document 152), the Atherton briefing (Document 155), the Akins–Sultan telegram (Document 161), Miki's letter (Volume E–12, Document 218) and the Tanaka telegram (Document 227); all are in the collection." Six documents cited by a short title and document number with no series name, years or history.state.gov link. Also line 94 "(Document 135 of the 1958–1960 Vietnam volume)" with no series name or link; line 135–136 "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume E–9, Part 1, Document 50)" with no link anywhere in the overview; and three documents quoted without any citation: "Vincent's February 1947 memorandum would vet each aid project for 'corrupt management'", "Ky told Lodge in 1966 that two corps commanders were corrupt", "the embassy urged Saigon to publicize the disciplining of 74 officials to 'meet criticism in the U.S.'". The overview holds 15 distinct history.state.gov links against the 28 documents of the collection it says it cites.

Part 3 states each gap as a search with its terms, scope and controls: "A search for the Church subcommittee under its three printed names found 24 documents in 15 volumes. A search for Lockheed with bribes, payoffs or payments found 43 documents in 20 volumes, 1957–1983... The Act's name appears in just four documents, in two volumes of 1978–1980, all after its passage... Every search ran over all 553 volumes. The positive control (\"Department of State\") was found in 552 of them; the one exception, a Paris Peace Conference volume of Council of Four minutes, does contain \"United States\". The negative control (a string that cannot occur) returned nothing." Two small gaps: the subcommittee's three printed names are not spelled out, and item (c), the pre-December-1910 limit of the citation data, is a measured tool limit ("About 300 nineteenth-century and early-twentieth-century documents that mention corruption therefore have no archival pointers here") rather than a search, and it says so ("That is a limit of the tools, not evidence that no records exist").

A grep of the overview for SQL keywords, table or column names (volume_id, document_id, body_text, user_content, table, column), file paths (/Users/, /tmp/, .db, .sqlite, .json) and any frus…/d… token outside a history.state.gov URL finds nothing. The only tool references are in prose: "A read-only copy of the FRUS Explorer search index (all 553 volumes) was searched" and "The editors' document and chapter headings were scanned in the TEI source files", neither a path, a table nor an id pair. Every id pair sits inside one of the 15 https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/ links.

judge:s8.rankingReason: s2: 19 documents in six findings from 1944 to 1980 (including bribery as an instrument of statecraft), every citation in full with a link, clean bullets, the most thorough account of what FRUS cannot give (post-1980 volumes searched, the subcommittee's 42 documents sifted to three, withheld names) and the most specific Read next. s8: the crispest three-part bottom line and the most readable findings, 28 documents with decade rates and a well-built collection (section prose, a note and excerpt per document, a threads-not-followed note), but about a third of its documents are cited short, unlinked or by description only, so the historian must go to the collection to reach them. s6: the most careful analytical answer (Koreagate as the one clear decision effect; admits it found no aid cut on corruption grounds alone) with every citation linked, but dense paragraphs of inline citations and a footnote channel that lists whole volumes' shelves rather than corruption material's. s1: a useful thematic grouping of 29 documents (reason for reform, risk to stability, American bribes, trust), but each finding dumps its quotations in a block after the prose and two of its cannot-get items are assertions rather than searches. s7: sound and fully cited, with the 1875 Venezuela case, but it rests on only eleven documents and its bottom line is one paragraph of inline citations; the thinnest evidence for the question.

score:s8.notes: All four files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), with a raw/ folder holding 16 scripts, their outputs and the 32 retrieved documents. Verification: every figure the memo publishes re-ran identically on the read-only copy (coverage 553|321749|1103|8481; corrupt* 2,186 of 311,429 in 399 volumes, 25 Ed2 hits dropped; brib* 658; Lockheed 43/20 with dates 1957-04-23 to 1983-04-19; FCPA 4/2; Church 24/15; American-personnel 76/54; black market 28/25; control 552 of 553 with frus1919Parisv05 at 90 rows and 89 for 'United States'; the false-friend table 5,222/294/1,779 and 306,207/1,892/92,045; the full decade table; 1,904 of 2,186 with a source row; external_citations' first date 1910-12-06; 297 dated hits before it, matching 'about 300'); the 28 pairs are present, non-apparatus, dated 1947-02-07 to 1978-08-26; all 22 quotations occur exactly once in their body_text; the came-from and pointed-at rows match the §3 tables; the lot resolutions (62D26 -> 1965953, 63D351/66D95 -> 2839192, 62D1 -> 2838992, 81D113 -> 1487627; 79F80 and 54D270 absent) match central-files-index.json and series-facts-index.json; the index, binary, map, .generation and both shards carry the one digest and documentOffset is 0.4; the overview's paraphrases of d50, d134, d161, d215, d218, d219 and d31 match the retrieved texts. The two violations: V8 (the overview's 'semantic vectors'; the d155 collection note's 'semantic neighbour') and O2' (the measured 552, 32, 9 of 2,186, about 300 and 12 volumes, plus several number-words, have no trace-table row, though each is in the memo's sections). Accuracy observations outside the items: the overview's Scope paragraph says '28 documents read in full' where the method shows three 260-character windows per match (the memo's 'retrieved whole ... read around every match' is the accurate wording); the bottom line says the Kennedy White House 'made' Korean aid conditional where d221 is an NSC-staff recommendation (Finding 3 itself says 'proposed'); the memo's 'all 28 argument pairs resolved' overstates vec.out's '27 of 27' (d155 joined after that run and was resolved by tier2.py), so the near-duplicate scan covered 27 of 28 (d155's volume has no second edition); the per-volume positive-control query counted apparatus rows without saying so; the stem probe for graft/kickback/embezzle was run but never reported. The O1 verdict reads an id pair inside a history.state.gov URL as a citation, as O4's wording does.

refute:s8.notes: WRONG CLAIMS FOUND (outside the five headline numbers, which all reproduce): (A) Overview Finding 1 and the collection's China prose: 'The China volumes of 1947 and 1948 hold more corruption documents than any other volumes.' Re-run of the per-volume corrupt* ranking (s_extras.out): frus1947v07 59 (1st), frus1894app2 40, frus1964-68v05 40, frus1958-60v01 37, frus1961-63v22 33, frus1948v07 32 (6th, tied with frus1969-76ve11p1). The 1948 volume is behind four others; the session's own raw/top_vols_corrupt.txt shows the same order. (B) Overview 'How this was done': 'Five episodes were chosen from the volumes where the word is densest' and memo §1 'chosen because they lead the per-volume ranking'. The 1974-76 episode's volumes do not: frus1969-76ve09p2 ranks 99th by count (6 hits) and 53rd by density, frus1969-76ve09p1 and ve15p2 233rd (2 hits each), frus1969-76ve12 36th (s_vol_ranks.out); that episode came from the heads scan and the Lockheed query, which the memo also says. (C) Memo §3.1: frus1969-76ve09p1/d50 is counted under the Central Foreign Policy File; its source is the Ford Library, NSA, NSC Operations Staff for the Middle East and South Asia Affairs, Box 18 (see identifierDetails). (D) Memo VECTORS item 4: 'every argument document' and 'within-set pairwise Hamming: mean 153.7' were computed over 27 documents (raw/vec.out: 'set rows resolved 27 of 27'), before d155 joined the set; over the 28 the mean is 152.9, min 52; d155 has no near-duplicate (nearest 69), so the conclusion stands. (E) Memo VECTORS item 1 lists exact neighbour orders that depend on an unstable sort at tied distances; distances and the named members reproduce (vectorUse). (F) Overview bottom line: 'the Kennedy White House made Korean aid conditional' cites frus1961-63v22/d221, which is an NSC staff recommendation by Robert H. Johnson to Rostow, not a decision; the quotation is exact. Every one of the 23 cited documents is returned by the corrupt*, brib* or Lockheed set and by at least one of the shorter printed lists (e.g. d628 by corrupt* and the China policy list; d122 by corrupt*, brib*, both Lockheed lists and the personnel query; d219 by corrupt* and Church; d50, d218, d227, d152 by brib* and both Lockheed lists). The three quoted-or-paraphrased uncited documents (d617, d134, d215) and the two collection-only documents (d583, d407) are returned by corrupt* and a printed list as well. Strict and practical readings coincide: no cited document reaches the overview through the vectors alone.
